children: The average asking price of newly listed properties rose 0.7%, or £2,441, during the month to £367,440, marking the first monthly increase since May. The rise was also slightly stronger than the average September increase of 0.5% recorded over the past decade.
However, asking prices remained 0.8% lower than a year earlier following several months of declines over the summer.
The number of new properties coming onto the market was flat compared with August and 3% lower than in September last year, Rightmove said.
Meanwhile, borrowing costs continued to rise, putting further pressure on affordability. The average two-year fixed mortgage rate increased to 5.29% from 5.09% a month earlier.

Rightmove property expert Colleen Babcock said: “September’s above-average price rise is a welcome sign of confidence after a particularly subdued summer, but it should be viewed as a modest recovery rather than a major turning point.”
She added that sellers faced “stiff competition” from the high number of homes already available and said realistic pricing remained important to secure a buyer.
